title.text: Budapest: Hungarian Wine Tasting with 8 Wines and Tapas

pills.pop_html: What's poured: Whites from cserszegi fűszeres (the "unpronounceable grape") and furmint, Hungary's best-known grape, then reds such as kadarka and Bull's Blood, from both larger and lesser-known producers. Works out at about €7.53 a wine.
On the plate: Olives, ham, sausages, tomatoes and several cheeses, all from farms just outside Budapest, served through the tasting along with bottled water.
Who leads it: A local wine expert and wine judge walks you through the history of Hungarian wine and its regions. You get tasting notes and a map of the wine regions.
Access: One of only two venues on this list marked wheelchair-accessible (the other is the Smúz Tokaji flight). Not suitable for under-18s or pregnant women.

best_for.pick_html: for a first proper Hungarian wine session, because it names its native grapes up front (cserszegi fűszeres, furmint, kadarka, Bull's Blood) with farm tapas included, at about €7.53 a wine.
best_for.skip_html: if Tokaji aszú is the one wine you came for: this line-up does not promise a sweet Tokaj, the Tasting Table sessions (#3, #6) do.

items.a: Wine the Gap, Tompa u. 26a, 1094 Budapest.
Guided tasting with a wine expert, 8 wines, tapas, bottled water, tasting notes, map of Hungary's wine regions.
Hotel pickup and drop-off.
No Tokaji aszú promised in the line-up. €11 more than the 8-wine Bortodoor tasting (#2). Hotel pickup not included.
8 wines from both big names and small producers. Farm tapas included, not a paid add-on. Native grapes most visitors never meet: cserszegi fűszeres, kadarka.

price.note: Free cancellation up to 24 hours before. The final price shows before you pay.

title.text: 8-Wine Hungarian Tasting in a Cosy City Centre Wine Bar

pills.pop_html: The line-up: 1 sparkling, 3 whites, 1 light red and 3 reds, bought directly from small local producers the bar works with. About €6.16 a wine, the lowest of the 8-wine tastings.
On the board: Local Hungarian cheeses, hams, salamis, olives and bread. A vegetarian board is available if you ask in advance; flag allergies when you book.
You leave with: A note page covering Hungary's wine regions, a wine-tasting how-to and space for your own tasting notes.
Pace: Two hours for 8 wines, about 15 minutes a glass, led by the bar's sommeliers. Transport to the bar is not included.

best_for.pick_html: for the best price per glass in town: 8 wines plus a charcuterie board for €49, about €6.16 a wine, in a District VI wine bar.
best_for.skip_html: if you want Tokaji: the 8 wines are sparkling, whites and reds, with no sweet wine listed.

Guided tasting with a sommelier, 1 sparkling and 7 still wines, charcuterie board with cheeses, meats and bread, take-home notes.
Transport.
No Tokaji or sweet wine in the line-up. Transport not included. Not suitable for under-18s.
Cheapest 8-wine tasting on the list. Sparkling, whites, light red and reds in one flight. Charcuterie board included, vegetarian on request.

title.text: Budapest: Essentials of Hungarian Wine Tasting Class

pills.pop_html: Running order: An aperitif, then whites and reds (sometimes a rosé), finishing with a sweet botrytised Tokaj aszú. Mostly from small producers, bought directly from winemakers the hosts know.
Why it matters: Aszú is Hungary's signature sweet wine and only 2 options here name it. This one pours it at the end of a full 8-wine class, at about €7.37 a wine.
On the plate: Pairings of local Hungarian delicacies plus mineral water, and tasting sheets with a map of the wine regions for notes.
When: Runs on most evenings from 6.00 to 8.00 pm. It needs at least 2 guests, otherwise you are offered another option or a full refund.

best_for.pick_html: for a structured evening class that ends on Tokaj aszú: a sommelier, 8 wines and food pairings at about €7.37 a glass.
best_for.skip_html: if you only have the afternoon free: it runs 6–8 pm. The sister tasting (#6) at the same address runs 3–5 pm.

items.a: Tasting Table Budapest, Bródy Sándor u. 9, 1088 Budapest.
Sommelier-led tasting, 8 wines, mineral water, food pairings, tasting sheets with a wine-region map.
Tips (optional).
Most evenings, 6.00–8.00 pm.
Evening slot only (6–8 pm). €10 more than Bortodoor's 8 wines. Needs a minimum of 2 guests to run.

title.text: Budapest: Half-Day Countryside Wine Tour with Meal and Transfer

pills.pop_html: Transport: Air-conditioned minibus from 11 selected central pick-up points (Hilton, Corinthia, InterContinental, Marriott and others) for the drive of about half an hour. Contact City & Wine before the day for your exact pickup time.
What's poured: 4 wines at each family-owned boutique winery, so 8–12 in all, with snacks and finger food in the cellars and time with the winemakers.
Lunch: A rustic 2-course home-cooked meal of classic Hungarian dishes at a local farm, with water. Vegetarian and gluten-free on request if you tell them before the tour.
Price maths: Transfers, wines, meal and an English-speaking guide for €85, about €7–11 a wine before you count the lunch and the drive. Tips are extra.

best_for.pick_html: for a countryside day without a car: hotel pickup, 2–3 family wineries in Etyek, 8–12 wines and a farm lunch for €85.
best_for.skip_html: if you have less than five hours: the city tastings pour 8 wines in 2 hours.

items.a: Selected central pick-up points, including Hilton Budapest, Corinthia, InterContinental, Four Seasons Gresham Palace, Marriott, Anantara New York Palace and the Hungarian State Opera.
Return minibus transfers, 4 wines at each winery, snacks in the cellars, home-cooked meal, water, English-speaking guide.
Tips.
Takes 4–5 hours of your day. Pickup only from 11 selected central points. 2-person minimum or you are moved to another date.
Hotel pickup and drop-off by air-conditioned minibus. 2–3 family wineries, 4 wines at each. Home-cooked Hungarian meal included.

price.note: Free cancellation up to 24 hours before. The final price shows before you pay.

title.text: From Budapest: Páty Wine Village Tour with Tastings

pills.pop_html: Group size: Capped at 8 people, the only wine tour here with a stated group limit. It needs at least 2 guests to run, or you are offered another date.
Where you taste: Páty's old wine cellars, some built as early as 1880, about a 20–30 minute drive from the centre. One of the wineries makes organic wine.

pills.summary_html: 🍷 4 wines per cellar▾
pills.pop_html: What's poured: At least 4 wines at each of 1 or 2 wineries, poured by the winemakers themselves, with plenty of time for questions.
Food: Olives, ham, sausages and several cheeses made by local farmers, served at the final cellar.

best_for.pick_html: for a small-group cellar visit: max 8 guests, winemakers pouring in 1880s cellars, 3 hours there and back from Erzsébet tér.
best_for.skip_html: if price per glass is what matters: at €96 for 4–8 wines it is the most expensive pour on this list.

items.a: Al Habtoor Palace Budapest, Erzsébet tér 9-10, 1051 Budapest.
Round-trip transfers by car, at least 4 wines at each cellar, tapas plate of olives, ham, sausages and local cheeses.
Max 8.
Most expensive option per wine. 1 or 2 wineries, so the wine count varies. Not suitable for under-18s.
Max 8 guests. Winemakers pour and answer questions themselves. Historic cellars, one winery organic.

price.note: Free cancellation up to 24 hours before. The final price shows before you pay.

title.text: Budapest: Wine, Cheese and Charcuterie Tasting

pills.pop_html: The line-up: 5 Hungarian wines with a focus on native grapes and local styles, ending with a glass of sweet wine from Tokaj. About €9.07 a wine.
On the board: Producer-sourced Mangalica pork sausage, water buffalo salami, smoked duck breast, grey beef sausage and several cheeses, plus bread and artisan oils.
When: Runs on most days from 3.00 to 5.00 pm, so it fits before dinner. A minimum of 2 guests is needed.
Price maths: The cheapest sommelier-led tasting on the list that includes a Tokaj sweet wine. Extra food or drinks are charged separately.

best_for.pick_html: for an afternoon slot with the best food on the list: Mangalica, buffalo salami and smoked duck with 5 wines ending on Tokaj, for €45.
best_for.skip_html: if you want more wines: €14 more buys the 8-wine evening class (#3) at the same venue.

items.a: Tasting Table Budapest, Bródy Sándor u. 9, 1088 Budapest.
5 glasses of Hungarian wine, cheese and charcuterie plate, bread and artisan oil, tasting sheets with a wine-region map.
Additional food or drinks, tips.
Most days, 3.00–5.00 pm.
Only 5 wines. Costs more per wine than the 8-wine bars. Extra food and drinks cost more.

title.text: Budapest: Tokaji Wine Tasting with Parliament Panorama

pills.pop_html: What's poured: 3 Holdvölgy Tokaji wines, including a sweet Aszú, from Hungary's most famous wine region. About €10.40 a glass.
Your seat: Reserved seating facing the Hungarian Parliament, on the terrace or at indoor tables, so it runs in any weather.
Food: Local cheeses, fresh fruit and snacks. Food and drinks beyond the tasting menu are charged separately.
Getting there: Tram 2 stops in front of the café at Parlament, látogatóközpont. Entry to the café's antique coffee-maker collection is included.

best_for.pick_html: for a Tokaji-only hour with the Parliament across the square, for €31.
best_for.skip_html: if you want a guided wine lesson: it is 3 wines poured by the café's host rather than a sommelier class.

items.a: Smúz Café, Kossuth Lajos tér 18, 1055 Budapest.
3 Holdvölgy Tokaji wines incl. Aszú, artisan platter, reserved seat with Parliament view, entry to the antique coffee-maker collection, English-speaking host.
Additional food and drinks, hotel pickup, tips.
Tram 2, Parlament, látogatóközpont stop.
Only 3 wines. Café host rather than a sommelier. New listing with few reviews so far.

price.note: Free cancellation up to 24 hours before. The final price shows before you pay.

title.text: Hungarian Pálinka Tasting: Discover Hungary's National Drink

pills.pop_html: What's poured: Nobilis Irsai Olivér grape (40%), Sáppusztai Piros Vilmos pear (42%) and Árpád Pálinkaház Dupla Kajszi apricot (60%).
Pour size: Each 2 cl measure is served in a tulip glass that concentrates the fruit aroma, 6 cl in all. About €6.53 a pour.
Food: Olives and water are included. A cheese and meat platter for two can be added at checkout, worth it before a 60% apricot finale.
Afterwards: The bar is a short walk from Gozsdu Courtyard and serves dinner, cocktails and over 200 drinks if you want to stay on.

best_for.pick_html: for Hungary's national spirit instead of wine: 3 premium pálinkas, from a 40% grape to a 60% apricot, for €20.
best_for.skip_html: if you want food included: only olives come with it, the platter costs extra.

items.a: Color Bar & Bistro, Madách Imre út 11, 1075 Budapest.
Guided tasting of 3 pálinkas (2 cl each), olives, water.
Hungarian, English.
Spirits only, no wine. Only olives included, platter extra. 60% finale is strong for beginners.
Cheapest option on the list. 3 premium pálinkas named in advance. Guided by a host in English or Hungarian.

title.text: Guided wine tasting at Rókusfalvy Estate

pills.summary_html: 🍾 4 wines or sparkling▾
pills.pop_html: What's poured: 4 Rókusfalvy wines or sparkling wines in the estate's press house, which seats up to 20. About €6.16 a glass.
Included: A short walk among the vines plus a look into the barrel cellar and the sparkling-wine cellar.
Food: Freshly baked scones and unlimited soft drinks. A cheese and ham tasting plate is available on request.
Getting there: No transfer is included: the estate is at Újhegy 89 in Etyek, though it can help you order one. Book at least 48 hours ahead.

best_for.pick_html: for travellers with a car already heading to Etyek: €25 at the winery itself, with a vineyard walk and cellar tour.
best_for.skip_html: if you need an English presentation or transport: it is presented in Hungarian and you get there on your own.

items.a: Rókusfalvy Estate, Újhegy 89, 2091 Etyek.
Guided tasting of 4 wines or sparkling wines, cellar tour, vineyard walk, freshly baked scones, unlimited soft drinks.
Hungarian.
Presentation in Hungarian. No transport included. Book 48 hours ahead.
Cheapest wine option on the list. Tasting at the winery itself. Vineyard walk and sparkling-wine cellar.
